spain-vs-denmark-1920-08-28.summary: Spain made its official international debut against Denmark in Brussels on 28 August 1920. Patricio Arabolaza scored the only goal of a 1–0 win.
spain-vs-denmark-1920-08-28.notes: The match took place at La Butte in Brussels. Some early accounts differ on venue details.

spain-vs-belgium-1920-08-29.summary: Spain lost 3–1 to hosts Belgium in the Olympic quarter-finals. Mariano Arrate scored Spain's goal from the penalty spot. Spain nevertheless continued in the tournament's consolation competition.
spain-vs-belgium-1920-08-29.notes: The 1920 tournament used an unusual medal-determination format after the main knockout rounds.

spain-vs-sweden-1920-09-01.summary: Spain defeated Sweden 2–1 in Antwerp. José María Belauste and Domingo Acedo scored as Spain advanced through the consolation competition.
spain-vs-sweden-1920-09-01.notes: Historical reports disagree on the venue and goal minutes. RSSSF discusses contemporary newspaper evidence about the stadium.

spain-vs-italy-1920-09-02.summary: Two goals from Félix Sesúmaga gave Spain a 2–0 victory over Italy in Antwerp, keeping the team in contention for an Olympic medal.
spain-vs-italy-1920-09-02.notes: The minute of Sesúmaga's second goal differs between historical sources; this summary deliberately omits it.

spain-vs-netherlands-1920-09-05.summary: Spain beat the Netherlands 3–1 in Antwerp to secure the silver medal. Félix Sesúmaga scored twice and Rafael Moreno, known as Pichichi, added the third.
spain-vs-netherlands-1920-09-05.notes: Czechoslovakia's disqualification affected the medal allocation and the consolation competition's format.
